##  {#recap data-menu-title="Recap"}

[Monday Recap]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Four join types:**
- `inner_join()` — only matches
- `left_join()` — all left + matching right
- `right_join()` — all right + matching left
- `full_join()` — everything

**Key insight:** Joins make statements about data relationships

**Today:** When those relationships don't match reality
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#why-joins-fail data-menu-title="Why Joins Fail"}

[Why Joins Fail]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Joins fail due to:**

1. **Mismatched keys** — values don't match exactly
2. **Missing keys** — NAs in key columns
3. **Duplicate keys** — unexpected one-to-many relationships
4. **Wrong join type** — doesn't match data structure
5. **Type mismatches** — numeric vs character keys

**All are detectable before or after joining**

**The key: ALWAYS validate your joins**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#validation-mindset data-menu-title="Validation Mindset"}

[The Validation Mindset]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Never assume a join worked correctly**

**Always check:**
- Row counts (before vs after)
- NA patterns (unexpected missingness?)
- Duplicates (unexpected row multiplication?)
- Key matches (did everything link?)

**Think of it like:** Checking your field data sheets for errors

**Defensive programming:** Catch problems early
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#row-count-check data-menu-title="Row Count Check"}

[Check 1: Row Counts]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Before join
nrow(birds)     # e.g., 1000 rows
nrow(sites)     # e.g., 20 rows

# Do the join
birds_joined <- birds %>%
  left_join(sites, by = "site")

# After join
nrow(birds_joined)

# Expected for left_join:
# Same as left table (1000) OR more if one-to-many

# If fewer: Something went wrong!
# If much more: Unexpected duplication!
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#row-count-interpretation data-menu-title="Row Count Interpretation"}

[Interpreting Row Count Changes]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**For `left_join()`:**
- Same rows? Good (one-to-one relationship)
- More rows? Check if expected (one-to-many on right)
- Fewer rows? ERROR — shouldn't happen with left join!

**For `inner_join()`:**
- Fewer rows? Expected (non-matches dropped)
- BUT: Know how many you expect to lose!

**For `full_join()`:**
- At least as many as larger table
- Could be more with multiple matches
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#unexpected-nas data-menu-title="Unexpected NAs"}

[Check 2: Unexpected NAs]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Check for NAs in joined columns
birds_joined %>%
  summarize(
    n_rows = n(),
    na_habitat = sum(is.na(habitat)),
    na_altitude = sum(is.na(altitude)),
    pct_na_habitat = mean(is.na(habitat)) * 100
  )

# Example result:
#   n_rows  na_habitat  na_altitude  pct_na_habitat
#   1000    150         150          15%

# 15% of birds have no site info!
# Question: Is this expected or an error?
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#na-interpretation data-menu-title="NA Interpretation"}

[Interpreting NAs After Joins]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**NAs in joined columns mean:** Key from left table didn't match anything in right table

**Could be legitimate:**
- New sites not yet in site database
- Observations at uncharacterized sites

**Could be an error:**
- Typo in site code
- Using wrong key column
- Site info under different name

**How to know:** Check WHICH sites have NAs
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#which-nas data-menu-title="Which NAs"}

[Finding Which Keys Didn't Match]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Which sites in birds have no match in sites?
birds_joined %>%
  filter(is.na(habitat)) %>%
  distinct(site) %>%
  pull(site)

# Example output:
# "site-C" "site-D" "sit_E"  "Site_F"

# Aha! Inconsistent naming:
# - "site-C" vs "site_C"  (dash vs underscore)
# - "sit_E" (typo)
# - "Site_F" (capitalization)
```
:::

::: body-text
**This tells you exactly what to fix!**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#anti-join-diagnostic data-menu-title="Anti Join Diagnostic"}

[Using `anti_join()` for Diagnosis]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Which birds were observed at sites NOT in the sites table?
unmatched_birds <- birds %>%
  anti_join(sites, by = "site")

# Check how many
nrow(unmatched_birds)  # How many birds?

# Which sites?
unmatched_birds %>%
  count(site)

# Which birds were at sites we DO have?
matched_birds <- birds %>%
  semi_join(sites, by = "site")

nrow(matched_birds)  # Should + above = total birds
```
:::

::: body-text
**Filtering joins reveal mismatches WITHOUT joining**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#duplicate-keys data-menu-title="Duplicate Keys"}

[Check 3: Duplicate Keys]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Are there duplicate keys in the RIGHT table?
sites %>%
  count(site) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

# Example:
#   site  n
#   A     1
#   B     3    <- B appears 3 times!
#   C     1

# This means:
# Every bird at site B will be duplicated 3x in the join!
```
:::

::: body-text
**Unexpected duplication is a common problem**

**Know your data structure!**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#expected-duplication data-menu-title="Expected Duplication"}

[Expected vs Unexpected Duplication]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Expected one-to-many:**
```r
# Multiple observations per site
observations %>% left_join(sites, by = "site")
# Each site info repeated for each observation
```

**Unexpected duplication:**
```r
# Sites table has duplicates (data entry error)
sites  # Should have unique site codes
#   site  habitat
#   A     forest
#   A     meadow   <- Duplicate site A!
```

**Always check if right table keys are unique when you expect one-to-one**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#checking-uniqueness data-menu-title="Checking Uniqueness"}

[Checking Key Uniqueness]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Check if keys are unique
sites %>%
  count(site) %>%
  summarize(
    total_rows = n(),
    unique_keys = n_distinct(site),
    has_duplicates = total_rows != unique_keys
  )

# OR with a helper function
check_unique_keys <- function(data, key_col) {
  data %>%
    count({{key_col}}) %>%
    filter(n > 1) %>%
    nrow() == 0  # TRUE if unique, FALSE if duplicates
}

check_unique_keys(sites, site)
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#type-mismatches data-menu-title="Type Mismatches"}

[Check 4: Key Column Types]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Check types of key columns
glimpse(birds)
# site: chr

glimpse(sites)
# site: num   <- Uh oh! Different types!

# This join will fail or create unexpected results

# Fix: Convert to same type
sites <- sites %>%
  mutate(site = as.character(site))

# OR
birds <- birds %>%
  mutate(site = as.numeric(site))
```
:::

::: body-text
**Keys must be the same type to match**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#validation-checklist data-menu-title="Validation Checklist"}

[Complete Join Validation Checklist]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Before joining:**
1. ✓ Check key column types (same type?)
2. ✓ Check for NAs in keys (will cause failed matches)
3. ✓ Check key uniqueness in right table (if expecting one-to-one)
4. ✓ Check for typos/inconsistencies in key values

**After joining:**
1. ✓ Check row count (expected change?)
2. ✓ Check for unexpected NAs (non-matches?)
3. ✓ Check for unexpected duplicates (row multiplication?)
4. ✓ Spot-check a few joined rows (look reasonable?)
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#validation-function data-menu-title="Validation Function"}

[Building a Join Validation Function]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
validate_join <- function(left, right, result, by) {
  cat("=== JOIN VALIDATION ===\n")
  cat("Left table rows:", nrow(left), "\n")
  cat("Right table rows:", nrow(right), "\n")
  cat("Result rows:", nrow(result), "\n")
  
  # Check duplication
  if(nrow(result) > nrow(left)) {
    cat("WARNING: Result has more rows than left table!\n")
  }
  
  # Check NAs
  na_count <- sum(is.na(result))
  if(na_count > 0) {
    cat("WARNING:", na_count, "NA values in result\n")
  }
  
  cat("======================\n")
}

# Use it:
result <- left_join(birds, sites, by = "site")
validate_join(birds, sites, result, "site")
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#fixing-typos data-menu-title="Fixing Typos"}

[Fixing Key Mismatches: Typos]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Problem: Inconsistent capitalization
birds %>% distinct(site)
# "Site_A", "site_B", "SITE_C"

sites %>% distinct(site)
# "site_a", "site_b", "site_c"

# Solution: Standardize case
birds_clean <- birds %>%
  mutate(site = tolower(site))

sites_clean <- sites %>%
  mutate(site = tolower(site))

# Now join will work
birds_clean %>%
  left_join(sites_clean, by = "site")
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#fixing-formats data-menu-title="Fixing Formats"}

[Fixing Key Mismatches: Formats]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Problem: Different separators
birds %>% distinct(site)
# "site-A", "site-B"

sites %>% distinct(site)
# "site_A", "site_B"

# Solution: Standardize format
birds_clean <- birds %>%
  mutate(site = str_replace(site, "-", "_"))

# OR fix the sites table
sites_clean <- sites %>%
  mutate(site = str_replace(site, "_", "-"))

# Now they match!
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#fixing-nas data-menu-title="Fixing NAs"}

[Handling NAs in Keys]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Problem: Some birds have NA for site
birds %>%
  count(is.na(site))
#   is.na(site)  n
#   FALSE        950
#   TRUE         50

# Option 1: Remove them before joining
birds_clean <- birds %>%
  filter(!is.na(site))

# Option 2: Replace NAs with a placeholder
birds_clean <- birds %>%
  mutate(site = replace_na(site, "unknown"))

# Then make sure sites table has "unknown"
sites <- sites %>%
  add_row(site = "unknown", habitat = NA, altitude = NA)
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#dealing-with-duplicates data-menu-title="Dealing with Duplicates"}

[Dealing with Duplicate Keys]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Problem: Sites table has duplicates
sites %>% count(site) %>% filter(n > 1)
#   site  n
#   A     2   <- Site A appears twice!

# View the duplicates
sites %>%
  filter(site == "A")
#   site  habitat    altitude
#   A     forest     250
#   A     forest     250    <- Exact duplicate? Remove it
# OR
#   A     forest     250
#   A     meadow     180    <- Different values? Which is correct?

# Solution 1: Remove exact duplicates
sites_clean <- sites %>%
  distinct()

# Solution 2: Keep first occurrence
sites_clean <- sites %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#compound-key-issues data-menu-title="Compound Key Issues"}

[Issues with Compound Keys]{.slide-title}

::: code-text
```r
# Compound key: site + date
birds %>%
  count(site, date) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
#   site  date        n
#   A     2024-01-15  2    <- Two birds at A on this date

# This is fine for one-to-many!
# But if joining to survey-level data:

surveys  # One row per site-date
#   site  date        observer
#   A     2024-01-15  Smith

birds %>%
  left_join(surveys, by = c("site", "date"))
# Each bird gets matched to the survey
# Both birds at site A on 2024-01-15 get observer = Smith
# This is correct!
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#join-workflow data-menu-title="Join Workflow"}

[Recommended Join Workflow]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**1. Explore both tables**
```r
glimpse(left_table)
glimpse(right_table)
```

**2. Check key columns**
```r
left_table %>% count(key) %>% filter(n > 1)
right_table %>% count(key) %>% filter(n > 1)
```

**3. Test with small sample**
```r
left_table %>% slice(1:5) %>%
  left_join(right_table, by = "key")
```

**4. Do full join and validate**
```r
result <- left_join(left_table, right_table, by = "key")
validate_join(left_table, right_table, result, "key")
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#common-mistakes data-menu-title="Common Mistakes"}

[Common Joining Mistakes]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**1. Forgetting to specify `by =`**
```r
# R joins on ALL matching column names
# Often not what you want!
```

**2. Not checking result**
```r
# Assuming it worked without validation
```

**3. Using inner_join() when you meant left_join()**
```r
# Silently drops non-matches
```

**4. Not handling NAs in keys**
```r
# NAs never match, even to other NAs
```

**5. Joining on wrong column**
```r
# site_id vs site_code — similar but different!
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#diagnosing-workflow data-menu-title="Diagnosing Workflow"}

[Diagnosing Failed Joins]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**When a join doesn't work:**

**Step 1:** Check row counts
- More/fewer than expected?

**Step 2:** Look for NAs
- Where are the non-matches?

**Step 3:** Use `anti_join()` to find non-matching keys
- Which keys don't match?

**Step 4:** Check those specific keys in both tables
- Typos? Format differences? Type mismatches?

**Step 5:** Fix and re-join

**Step 6:** Validate the fixed join
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#thinking-exercise data-menu-title="Thinking Exercise"}

[Thinking Exercise]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**You join bird observations to site data:**

```r
result <- birds %>% 
  left_join(sites, by = "site")
```

**You find:**
- 1000 birds → 1200 rows in result
- Many habitat values are NA

**What could be wrong?**

Think through the diagnosis before advancing
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#thinking-answer data-menu-title="Thinking Answer"}

[Thinking Exercise: Answer]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**1200 rows (more than 1000):** Unexpected duplication
- Check: `sites %>% count(site) %>% filter(n > 1)`
- Likely: Some sites appear multiple times in sites table

**Many NAs in habitat:** Non-matches
- Check: Which sites? `result %>% filter(is.na(habitat)) %>% count(site)`
- Then: `birds %>% anti_join(sites, by = "site")`
- Likely: Typos or sites not in sites table

**Fix both issues:**
- Remove duplicate sites (or figure out which is correct)
- Fix site name typos in birds table
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#real-world data-menu-title="Real World"}

[Real-World Join Debugging]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**In practice:**
- First join attempt often reveals data quality issues
- This is GOOD — you're finding problems!
- Iterative process: join → diagnose → fix → re-join
- Document fixes in your code
- Keep original data unchanged (fix in pipeline)

**Example comment:**
```r
# Fix known typo: site "site-C" should be "site_C"
birds_clean <- birds %>%
  mutate(site = if_else(site == "site-C", "site_C", site))
```

**The join IS data quality control**
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#documentation data-menu-title="Documentation"}

[Documenting Join Decisions]{.slide-title}

::: body-text
**Always document:**

**Why this join type:**
```r
# Using left_join to keep all observations
# even if site metadata is missing
```

**What you expect:**
```r
# Expect 1-to-1 relationship (no row duplication)
# Sites table should have unique site codes
```

**Any data fixes:**
```r
# Standardized site codes to lowercase
# to match sites table format
```

**Validation results:**
```r
# Validated: All 1000 observations matched
# No unexpected NAs or duplication
```
:::
